hints: Notice the question asks how a stationary pattern with fixed nodes and antinodes can be built from travelling progressive waves.
Recall that when two waves meet, the resultant displacement at each point is the vector sum of the two separate displacements.
Compare adding two identical waves travelling in opposite directions with diffraction spreading, polarisation filtering, and Doppler frequency shift.
walkthrough: Identify the key feature: a stationary wave has points of zero displacement called nodes and points of maximum oscillation called antinodes, with no net transfer of energy.
Recall the usual way this is produced: a progressive wave reflects back on itself, so two progressive waves of the same wavelength and frequency travel in opposite directions through the same region.
State the governing rule: the principle of superposition says resultant displacement $y = y_1 + y_2$ at every point and instant.
Apply the rule: where the two waves are always in antiphase they cancel to give a node, and where they are always in phase they reinforce to give an antinode.
Conclude that superposition of oppositely travelling progressive waves explains the stationary wave, which is option C.

options.A: Diffraction is the spreading of a wave through a gap or around an obstacle and does not combine two oppositely travelling waves to make nodes and antinodes.
options.B: Polarisation restricts the vibration direction of a transverse wave and does not add displacements of two progressive waves together.
options.C: Two progressive waves of the same frequency travelling in opposite directions add by the principle of superposition to give fixed nodes and antinodes.
options.D: The Doppler effect is the change in observed frequency due to relative motion of source and observer, not the formation of a stationary wave pattern.
